indication: [AGE]-year-old [GENDER], 10 days status post bilateral DIEP flap breast reconstruction. Presents with left chest pain and clinical evidence of skin necrosis. Evaluate for operative site abscess.
technique: ** Helical CT acquisition was performed from the thoracic inlet through the upper abdomen following the administration of intravenous contrast. Multiplanar reformats were reviewed.
findings:
**
The lungs are clear without evidence of consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. There is no suspicious pulmonary nodule identified. The trachea and mainstem bronchi remain patent. The mediastinal contours are within normal limits; there is no significant lymphadenopathy in the axillary or hilar regions. The heart size is normal and the pericardium is thin without effusion.
Regarding the surgical sites, there is evidence of bilateral breast reconstruction utilizing free flaps. On the right side, the flap appears well-perfused with no abnormal fluid collections. On the left side, there is an area of decreased enhancement involving the superficial aspect of the flap, consistent with the known skin necrosis. There is some mild subcutaneous edema and stranding in the surrounding soft tissues. However, there is no organized fluid collection, rim-enhancing pocket, or internal gas bubbles to suggest a formal abscess at the operative site. The underlying pectoralis muscle and deep fascial planes are unremarkable.
Incidental findings include a small, simple 5mm cyst in the visualized portion of the liver. There is also a prominent azygos vein, which is a normal anatomical variant. The visualized adrenal glands and upper abdominal organs are otherwise unremarkable.
conclusion:
**
Post-operative changes following bilateral DIEP flap reconstruction. There is evidence of necrosis of the left flap as described, but no CT evidence of an associated operative site abscess.
